I’ve made ten jars like this, crimson pots, thrown crimson clay that’ll eventually be coated in a crimson glaze and then finally, they’ll be reduction fired, oh, there’s also some bronze in the mix, small fragments, which when put through the kiln turn into these red haloed flecks of metal. All of that might sound quite over the top but it’s a deep red with underlying tones of black and hopefully they resemble some of the tests I’ve fired in the past… fingers crossed. They require a different approach when crafting them, especially during the turning stage. As the particles of grog the body contains are constantly torn out I have to go back over the surface, burnishing it and smoothing it as I go to get rid of the overly prominent scratches these splinters of ceramic create. I lost a few pieces from attempting to fix oval openings, they were thrown round, but as clay slowly dries it’s quite common for it to subtlety warp. I tried to gentle press the opening back into a round shape and I felt something give; upon further inspection I found a hairline crack in the rim. Grogged clays might be tough during the throwing and the firing but it’s brittle stuff during the trimming stage, especially when trimmed as thinly as this. #clay #handmade #satisfying #pottery #ceramics

This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. So tell me, what makes you stay hopeful when life feels extra gloopy? #ceramicartist #dopaminedecor #glitterinlay #rainbowart #processvideo

Did you know that you are not limited just by the size of your kiln when making large ceramics! The best way to build big pottery in my opinion his with coils. I’m making a floor lamp for a client and decided that stacking multiple pieces was how I was going to get the hight required for a piece of clay furniture! I love how that pottery really is just using the same dozen or so techniques in a bunch of different combinations, and that your creativity can allow you to really break through what is “possible”. This is only one piece in a huge series of lighting and showroom decor for the new Elliott Cole Home by Basecamp Design! I cannot wait to share more and show everything in the space soon. lidded jar tutorial - part 1 (throwing the jar body and lid)✨ have to break this up into 3 parts because it will take weeks to go through the steps (we're making these jars in real time and rely on a community studio to fire) and I simply can't fit throwing, trimming, and glazing the jars into one reel 🥲 i find 200g is perfect for throwing the small jar body, plus another 150g for the lid. you'll see i throw my jar body and lid separately, leaving a lot of the refining for the trimming stage. especially with the lids, I find it easier to throw them roughly and finesse the fit once they're leather hard. i don't wire off the lids or jars, i wait until they pop off the bats. xo shan #pottery #potterytutorial #liddedjar #handmadeceramics #canadianartist

I can take myself seriously as an artist without believing that a gallery, residency, MFA, collector, or critic makes my work inherently more important than someone making extraordinary pots as their everyday trade. Here’s a completed apothecary jar and a full overview of how it’s made. For this type of lidded jar, the base and lid are thrown from one continuous piece of clay, then cut open and trimmed to create the inner edges and gallery so the lid doesn’t slide off. I like this type of piece because it has a continuous line from the base to the top of the knob. It’s a very elegant shape and one I imagine would look lovely on a shelf holding trinkets, spices, or chocolates. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #handmade #potteryartist

Colanders, strainers, even berry bowls are quite popular. I make a few types of small medium and large colanders, but have really enjoyed making these strainer bowls. The shape is more of a basket or bassinet in which the strainer holes are only at the upper half of the bowl. This allows the fruit or veggies to be fully submerged in water before tipping and pouring out without spilling the produce. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #berrybowl #potteryartist
